node.title: Re: So what is your Perl book "Trilogy" anyway? (Perl Book References)
node.author: eyepopslikeamosquito
node.doctext:
My three favourite Perl books:

  1. Camel (Programming Perl)
  2. Shiny Ball (Effective Perl Programming)
  3. Staghound (Perl Best Practices)

See also:

  • perl.org free online Perl books
  • [id://23304] (Perl Monks Book Reviews section)

For a long list of links for getting started with Perl see:

  • [id://1172735]

Extra Book References Added Later

Some Perl book lists:

  • learn.perl.org - basic book list (see especially Learning Perl by [merlyn])
  • perl.org - longer book list (all books mostly free)
  • 50 Best Perl Books of All Time - bookauthority.org (suspect commercial Perl book list)

Some Perl book and other recommendations:

  • Modern Perl - by [chromatic], fantastic free intro to Perl for decent programmers who are not familiar with perl (Modern Perl book web site by [chromatic] (updated for perl 5.22, 2016) is on an indefinite hiatus)
  • perlmaven (by [szabgab] - lots of good free stuff here)
  • Perl Taster (Kindle) (by [davorg] - not free but very cheap)

  • Effective Perl Programming by brian d foy et al
  • Minimal Perl by Tim Maher
